- When sentiment is consistently negative (0.00 or low) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 3–5% relative to recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or adjust downward by 2–4% per day post-spike.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion — add a 1–2% downward bias to forecast if sentiment >0.5 and price >10% below 5-day moving avg.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the window (first 5–7 days) — apply 2–3% downward adjustment to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting next 5 days.
